title: I built a trading decision practice tool — looking for a few early testers with trading experience
author: EntertainerNew7911
selftext: Hey, I built Integrilis, a tool for practicing trading decisions without knowing what happens next. You get a historical market setup with the future hidden, make your decision first, then reveal what happened and review it after. I'm looking for a few people with trading experience who are willing to actually try it and tell me what feels confusing, what doesn't help, what breaks, or what you'd change. It's not signals, predictions or financial advice. It's just for practice. Public signup isn't open yet, so I'm giving access manually for now. If you're interested, comment here or DM me.

comments.author: Godzillaton
comments.body: i think its best you directly show what you built here. care to share the link or something?

replies.author: EntertainerNew7911
replies.body:
Sure, this is it:

[https://integrilis.com](https://integrilis.com)

Public signup isn't open yet, so if you want to actually try it, send me a DM and I'll set up access for you.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: The reveal is the part I'd be careful with. If you show what happened using the close, people learn to size off a price they'd never have gotten. Show the fill they'd actually have taken, worst side of the spread, and the lesson survives contact with a real broker.

replies.author: EntertainerNew7911
replies.body:
Fair point on the spread side of execution realism. One clarification though: Integrilis doesn’t use the reveal close as the trade fill.

The planned entry and the simulated fill are separate. With the daily OHLC data we use today, if price gaps through a stop entry, the fill moves to the actual daily open rather than pretending the trader got the original trigger price. If the level is touched normally, it fills at the planned level.

Stops and targets are also resolved from the candle range, not from the close. If both SL and TP are reachable inside the same daily candle, we deliberately take the conservative outcome because daily data can’t tell us which happened first.

What we don’t model in V1 is broker-specific bid/ask spread, slippage, liquidity or tick-level execution. That part of your point is fair, and it’s a known boundary of the current version.

Higher-granularity intraday execution is something we can add later. Right now I want to validate the actual training loop first — decision before outcome, then review the evidence after.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body:
with daily bars the case that gets people is the same day one: if the entry stop and the protective stop both sit inside one day's range, OHLC won't tell you which was hit first, so the sim has to guess and it tends to guess kindly.

we ended up marking those days unresolved rather than picking an order.

replies.author: EntertainerNew7911
replies.body:
Yeah, that’s the same ambiguity we had to deal with.

We made a slightly different choice. We don’t resolve that case kindly — if the daily bar makes the entry and the protective stop both reachable and the intraday order can’t be known from OHLC, the resolver takes the conservative path rather than giving the trader the benefit of the doubt. Same idea if SL and TP are both reachable in one daily candle: we score the loss.

Marking it unresolved is a valid design choice too. We chose deterministic conservative resolution so the training loop can still complete consistently until we add higher-granularity intraday data.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: Same call we made, we take the worst side of every spread, always. The one cost worth knowing: on a practice tool, always scoring the loss teaches someone their entry was worse than it really was. Fine for grading, less fine for training. Do you show them the bar was ambiguous?

replies.author: EntertainerNew7911
replies.body:
Good catch. I checked the actual UI after your comment and you were right — we were recording the ambiguity correctly, but we weren’t explaining it clearly enough to the trader.

Fixed now.

When both SL and TP are reachable inside the same Daily candle, we still score the trade conservatively as a loss, but the UI now explicitly says that Daily OHLC can’t tell which level was hit first and explains why the loss was assigned.

So the grading stays conservative, but the trader now sees the ambiguity instead of just getting the result.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: the same-candle case is where most practice tools quietly flatter the trader, so scoring it conservatively is the right default. worth surfacing the ambiguity in the UI too, not just folding it into the score.

replies.author: EntertainerNew7911
replies.body: Yep — that’s exactly what we changed after your comment. The conservative score stays, but the UI now explicitly flags the same-candle ambiguity and explains that Daily OHLC can’t determine which level was hit first.
